claims.text: Treccani describes Naples’s unequal civic representation, with one popular representative against five nobles. TDV describes Tunis’s sultan-selected consultation, divans and qadi offices within the Hafsid setting. These are different constituencies and governing institutions, not powers supplied by a capital or dynasty label. The retrospectives leave originals uncollated and do not make every office unchanged across all reigns. The library dates Aragonese succession to 1442; the institute distinguishes arrival from 1443 rebuilding of the royal residence. These are separate acts.

claims.text: Why does a representative institution not establish equal civic power? Naples’s one-to-five representation is unequal, and Tunis’s described consultation and appointments follow a separate court relation. Aragonese succession/residence and rebuilding add separately dated 1442/1443 acts, not identical civic powers or an exact conquest day.

A representative body gives all residents equal civic power.
